pp:ce:2024:q32.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 32
pp:ce:2024:q32.question:
A flow velocity field $\vec{V}: \vec{V}(x, y)$ for a fluid is represented by
$\vec{V}=3 \tilde{\hat{i}}+(5 x) \hat{j}$
In the context of the fluid and the flow, which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: The fluid is incompressible and the flow is rotational.
The fluid is incompressible and the flow is irrotational.
The fluid is compressible and the flow is rotational.
The fluid is compressible and the flow is irrotational

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Fluid Kinematics
detailed_solution.markdown:
Continuity equation for incompressible flow :

$$\begin{aligned}

\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & =0 \\

\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(3)+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(5 x) & =0+0 \\

& =0 \text { (Incompressible Flow) } \\

\omega_{z} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}(5 x)-\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(3)\right] \\

& =\frac{1}{2}(5)=2.5 \neq 0 \text { (Flow is rotational) }

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2024:q33.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 33
pp:ce:2024:q33.question: For assessing the compliance with the emissions standards of incineration plants, correction needs to be applied to the measured concentrations of air pollutants. The emission standard (based on $11 \%$  Oxygen) for $\mathrm{HCl}$ is $50 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{Nm}^{3}$ and the measured concentrations of $\mathrm{HCl}$ and Oxygen in flue gas are $42 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{Nm}^{3}$ and $13 \%$ , respectively. Assuming $21 \%$  Oxygen in air, the CORRECT statement is:
options: No compliance, as the corrected $\mathrm{HCl}$ emission is greater than the emission standard.
Compliance is there, as the corrected $\mathrm{HCl}$ emission is lesser than the emission standard
Compliance is there, as there is no need to apply the correction since Oxygen is greater than $11 \%$  and $\mathrm{HCl}$ emission is lesser than the emission standard.
No compliance, as the Oxygen is greater than $11 \%$  in the flue gas.

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Air and Noise Pollution
detailed_solution.markdown:
As per $\mathrm{CPCB}$, oxygen correction factor is calculated as shown below-

$E_{s}=\frac{\left(21-0_{s}\right) E_{m}}{21-0_{m}}$

Where

$E_{s}=$  Calculated emission concentration in $\%$  at the standard percentage oxygen concentration in %

$E_{m}=$  Measured emission concentration in %

$\mathrm{O}_{s}=$  Standard oxygen concentration in %

$\mathrm{O}_{m}=$  Measured oxygen concentration in %

Note: This correction is done only when measured % oxygen concentration is higher than standard % oxygen (i.e. $11 \%$  )

So,

$E_{s}=\frac{21-11}{21-13} \times 42=52.5 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{Nm}^{3}$

Hence, no compliance, the corrected $\mathrm{HCl}$ emission is greater than emission standard i.e. $50 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{Nm}^{3}$.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2024:q38.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ce:2024:q38.question:
A $2 \mathrm{~m} \times 2 \mathrm{~m}$ tank of $3 \mathrm{~m}$ height has inflow, outflow and stirring mechanisms. Initially, the tank was half filled with fresh water. At $t=0$, an inflow of salt a solution of concentration $5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ at the rate of 2 litre/s and an outflow of the well stirred mixture at the rate of 1 litre/s are initiated. This process can be modeled using the following differential equation.
$\frac{d m}{d t}+\frac{m}{6000+t}=0.01$
where $m$ is the mass (grams) of salt at time $t$ (seconds). The mass of the salt (in grams) in the tank at $75 \%$ of its capacity is ______(rounded off to 2 decimal places).

primary.subtopicLabel: Precipitation and General Aspects of Hydrology

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Precipitation and General Aspects of Hydrology
detailed_solution.markdown:
Total capacity of tank $=2 \times 2 \times 3=12 \mathrm{~m}^{3}$

At $50 \%$  capacity,

$\text { Volume }\left(V_{50}\right)=0.5 \times 12=6 \mathrm{~m}^{3}$

At $75 \%$  capacity,

$\text { Volume }\left(V_{75}\right)=0.75 \times 12 \mathrm{~m}^{3}=9 \mathrm{~m}^{3}$

Now, increase in volume $\Delta V=V_{75}-V_{50}=(9-6) \mathrm{m}^{3}=3 \mathrm{~m}^{3}$

Also,

$\text { Inflow }(I)=2 \mathrm{l} / \mathrm{s}$

Outflow $(Q)=1 \mathrm{l} / \mathrm{s}$

Rate of change storage,

$$\begin{aligned}

\frac{\Delta S}{\Delta t} & =I-Q=2-1=1 \mathrm{l} / \mathrm{s} \\

& =\frac{3000 l}{1 \mathrm{l} / \mathrm{s}}=3000 \mathrm{sec}

\end{aligned}$$

Now,

$\frac{d m}{d t}+\frac{m}{6000+t}=0.01$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d m}{d t}+\frac{m}{6000+3000}=0.01$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d m}{d t}+\frac{m}{9000}=0.01$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d m}{0.01-\frac{m}{9000}}=d t$

Integrating both sides

$\Rightarrow \quad \int_{m_{0}=0}^{m} \frac{d m}{0.01-\frac{m}{9000}}=\int_{t=0}^{t=3000} d t$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\left[\ln \left(0.01-\frac{m}{9000}\right)\right]_{0}^{m}}{-\frac{1}{9000}}=(3000-0)$

$\Rightarrow \quad \ln \left(0.01-\frac{m}{9000}\right)-\ln 0.01=-\frac{1}{9000} \times 3000$

$$\begin{array}{rlrl}

\Rightarrow & & \ln \left(0.01-\frac{m}{9000}\right) & =-4.938 \\

\Rightarrow & 0.01-\frac{m}{9000} & =7.165 \times 10^{-3} \\

\Rightarrow & m & =25.5 \mathrm{gm}

\end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **25** (acceptable range: [24.5, 25.5]).

pp:ce:2024:q40.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:ce:2024:q40.question:
An inverted T-shaped concrete beam (B1) in the figure, with centroidal axis $X-X$ is subjected to an effective prestressing force of $1000 \mathrm{kN}$ acting at the bottom kern point of the beam cross-section. Also consider an identical concrete beam (B2) with the same grade of concrete but without any prestressing force.

The additional cracking moment (in $\mathrm{KNm}$ ) that can be carried by beam $\mathrm{B} 1 \mathrm{~m}$ comparison to beam B2 is ______ (rounded off to the nearest integer).

detailed_solution.markdown:
At bottom fibre,

$\frac{P}{A}+\frac{P e y_{b}}{I}-\frac{M_{c r}}{I} y_{b}=0 \;\;\;...(i)$

where

$$\begin{aligned}

P & =\text { Prestressing force } \\

e & =\text { Eccentricity of P-force } \\

M_{c r} & =\text { cracking moment for beam B1 }

\end{aligned}$$

$y_{t}$ and $y_{b}$ are distance of top and bottom fibre from neutral axis respectively, At top fibre

$\frac{P}{A}-\frac{P e y_{t}}{I}=0$

[P-force is at kern point]

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{I}{A}=e y_{t}  \;\;\;...(ii)$

Putting (ii) in (i)

$$\begin{aligned}

\frac{M_{c r}}{I} y_{b} & =\frac{P}{A}+\frac{P e y_{t}}{I} \\

\Rightarrow \quad M_{c r} & =\frac{P I}{A y_{b}}+P e \\

& =\frac{P e y_{t}}{y_{b}}+P e \\

& =\frac{P e(2 H / 3)}{(H / 3)}+P e \\

& =3 P e=3 \times 1000 \times \frac{100}{1000}=300 \mathrm{kNm}

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **300** (acceptable range: [299, 301]).

pp:ce:2024:q41.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:ce:2024:q41.question: The initial cost of an equipment is Rs. 1,00,000. Its salvage value at the end of accounting life of 5 years is Rs. 10,000. The difference in depreciation (in Rs.) computed using 'double-declining balance method' and 'straight line method' of depreciation in Year-2 is ____ (in positive integer)

detailed_solution.concept: Construction Materials and Management - Construction Materials and Management
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given:

Initial cost,

$C_{i}  =\text { Rs. } 1,00,000$

Salvage value,

$C_{s}  =\text { Rs. } 10,000$

Useful life, $n  =5 \text { years }$

Straight line method,

Depreciation,

$$\begin{aligned}

D & =\frac{C_{i}-C_{s}}{n} \\

& =\frac{10^{5}-10^{4}}{5} \\

& =\text { Rs. } 18,000

\end{aligned}$$

As per double declining method,

Fixed factor, $\quad$ FDDB $=\frac{2}{n}=\frac{2}{5}=0.4$

$$\begin{aligned}

\therefore \quad \text { Book value, } D_{1} & =\text { FDDB } \times C_{i}=0.4 \times 1,00,000=40,000 \text { Rs } \\

B_{1} & =\text { Rs. } 1,00,000-\text { Rs. } 40,000=\text { Rs. } 60,000 \\

D_{2} & =\text { FDDB } \times B_{1}=0.4 \times 60,000 \\

& =\text { Rs. } 24,000

\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \quad$ Difference in depreciation $= \text { Rs. } 24,000-  \text { Rs. } 18,000

=\text { Rs. } 6000$

Therefore, the correct answer is **6000**.

pp:ce:2024:q43.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 43
pp:ce:2024:q43.question: The total primary consolidation settlement $\left(S_{C}\right)$ of a building constructed on a $10 \mathrm{~m}$ thick saturated clay layer is estimated to be $50 \mathrm{~mm}$. After 300 days of the construction of the building. primary consolidation settlement was reported as $10 \mathrm{~mm}$. The additional time (in days) required to achieve $50 \%$  of $S_{c}$ will be ____ (rounded off to the nearest integer).

detailed_solution.markdown:
As we know, $\quad\left(T_{v}\right)_{50}=\frac{C_{v} t}{d^{2}} \quad$  where, $C_{v}$ is coefficient of consolidation

$\frac{\pi}{4}(0.5)^{2}=\frac{C_{v}}{d^{2}} \times t_{2}$

For $10 \mathrm{~mm}$ settlement, $\% U=\frac{\Delta h}{\Delta H} \times 100=\frac{10}{50} \times 100 \%=20 \%$

$$\begin{aligned}

\left(T_{v}\right)_{20} & =\frac{C_{v}}{d^{2}} \times t \\

\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\pi}{4}(0.2)^{2} & =\frac{C_{v}}{d^{2}} \times 300 \\

\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\frac{\pi}{4}(0.5)^{2}}{\frac{\pi}{4}(0.2)^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{C_{v}}{d^{2}} \times t_{2}}{\frac{C_{v}}{d^{2}} \times 300} \\

\Rightarrow \quad t_{2} & =\left(\frac{0.5}{0.2}\right)^{2} \times 300=1875 \text { days }

\end{aligned}$$

Additional number of days $=(1875-300)$ days $=1575$  days

Therefore, the correct answer is **1575** (acceptable range: [1550, 1600]).

pp:ce:2024:q50.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:ce:2024:q50.question:
Activated carbon is used to remove a pollution from wastewater in a mixed batch reactor, which follows first-order reaction kinetics.
At a reaction rate of 0.38 /day, the time (in days) required to remove the pollutant by $95 \%$ is ______ (rounded off to 1 decimal place).

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
For first order kinetics,

$N_{t}=N_{0} e^{-k t}$

For efficiency of $95 \%$,

$$\begin{aligned}

N_{t} & =\left(1-\frac{95}{100}\right)^{L_{0}} \\

& =0.05 N_{0}

\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \quad 0.05=e^{-0.38 t}$

Taking In on both sides,

$$\begin{array}{ll}

& \ln 0.05  =-0.38 t \times \operatorname{lne} \\

\Rightarrow  &t  =7.9 \text { days }

\end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **7.9** (acceptable range: [7.8, 8]).

pp:ce:2024:q58.title: GATE CE 2024 | Set 1 | Question: 58
pp:ce:2024:q58.question: For positive integers $\mathrm{p}$ and $\mathrm{q}$, with $\frac{\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{q}} \neq 1\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{\frac{p}{q}}=p^{\left(\frac{p}{q}-1\right)}$. Then,

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, $p > 0, q > 0$ and $\frac{p}{q} \neq 1$

$$\begin{array}{rlrl}

& \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{p / q} & =p^{\left(\frac{p}{q}-1\right)} \\

& \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{p / q} & =p^{\left(\frac{p-q}{q}\right)} \\

& \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^p & =p^{q-q} \\

& \therefore & \left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^p & =\frac{p^p}{p^q} \\

q^p & =p^q

\end{array}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.
